saints.name: The Dedication of the Basilica of St. Mary Major
saints.title: Our Lady of the Snows
saints.shortBlurb: The commemoration of the great Roman basilica raised in Our Lady's honor on the Esquiline Hill…
biography: This day commemorates the dedication of the Basilica of St. Mary Major on Rome's Esquiline Hill, the oldest church in the West raised in honour of the Mother of God and one of the four papal basilicas. It is also called St. Mary of the Crib, for its relic of the Lord's manger.

A tradition first recorded after the year 1000 gives the feast its older name, Our Lady of the Snows: in the days of Pope Liberius, a childless patrician named John and his wife vowed their fortune to the Virgin, and on the night of 5 August snow fell on the summit of the Esquiline, marking where a church should rise.

The present basilica was built by Pope Sixtus III in the years after the Council of Ephesus of 431, which had solemnly proclaimed Mary Theotokos, the Mother of God. Its dedicatory inscription proclaims 'Sixtus the bishop to the people of God.'

Its fifth-century mosaics, on the triumphal arch and along the nave, are among the oldest monuments of Marian art. The feast entered the General Roman Calendar in 1568 as the Dedication of St. Mary of the Snows and received its present name in 1969.
saints.knownFor: The oldest Marian basilica in the West.
